newsitem.title: NORWAY: Christiania, Storebrand jump on merger.
newsitem.headline: Christiania, Storebrand jump on merger.

text.p: Shares in Norway's second largest commercial bank, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA, and in the country's largest insurance company, Storebrand ASA, jumped in early trade in Wednesday after the two announced they planned to merge.

At 0851 GMT Storebrand had advanced more than seven percent to 48.60 crowns in turnover of 55.7 million, while Christiania Bank was almost five percent up at 25.50 crowns in business worth 35.4 million crowns.

The new company, to be called Christiania Group, will have a market capitalisation of about 26 billion crowns and will be Norway's largest financial group and will be the sixth largest in the Nordic region, according to a joint statement.

Soon after the announcement, the Oslo bourse said it had transferred both companies to an observation list for close monitoring, a routine practise when mergers or extraordinary announcements are made.
